kitDescription: Exia (Treasure) is an Electric Supporter sniper (Burst I, 20s) whose value is mostly team support. Each full-charge shot builds a Collect Hacking Code stack, raising her own ATK by 28% per stack up to five. When her magazine's last round lands while she holds a code, all Electric allies (herself included) gain an ATK buff equal to 5.8% of her ATK, stacking to five. On entering any Full Burst her reload speed is fixed at +95% for 10 seconds, and her last bullet also debuffs the boss's ATK and DEF (both inert on the sim's no-boss-damage, DEF=0 basis and recorded as unmodeled). Her burst hits the boss for 122.32% of final ATK with a small DEF shred, and when fired at max Hacking Code stacks it lands a second 122.32% hit and makes the boss take +18.04% damage from the whole team for 10 seconds.

verdictRationale: All nine kit lines are FAITHFUL (6) or DOCUMENTED_GAP (3: the enemy ATK▼/DEF▼ lines, unenactable at the sim's DEF=0 no-boss-damage basis and carried verbatim in unmodeled with the correct reason — S2b's load-bearing DEF▼ call is reconciled, and S5's own skips plus S6's identical dispositions corroborate). The S5 blind suite runs RED (13/20), but every failure classifies as a blind-side artifact, not a driver divergence: two engine-channel assertions demanding buffApply events the enemy-debuff path never emits, two encoding-shape mismatches (the driver's resource-pool + perResource Collect Hacking Code is semantically the blind's atkPct maxStacks-5, and the driver pins the ramp behaviorally at the exact 2.4× ratio), three no-op counterfactuals (ov[slot].blocks on flat-array slots), and six fixture contaminations/dynamics (liter's reload, crown's casterAtkPct, helm's durationShots, and a two-B1 comp where the max-stack gate closure can never appear). Convergence here is the weak kind — same-model agreement — so the meaningful signals are the divergences, and the real one runs in the driver's favor: S6 shipped the burst rider UNGATED while the prose says 'at max stacks', and the driver's fixture proves its gate (pre-max opener lands one hit, post-max casts land two). The driver's own suite discriminates under every named nearest-wrong model (no-stacks, instant-max, all-allies, no-reload, no-taken) with correctly-shaped patches. Residual same-model risks for owner spot-check, all documented ⚑ rather than gotchas: (a) stack-duration refresh-vs-independent-timer semantics on both stacking lines (driver holds 5 stacks; an independent-timer game would settle near ~2 on the 15s share — board A/B is the outer check); (b) the never-decaying hackingCode pool (identical at continuous 1.37s cadence, diverges only after >5s of not firing); (c) the additive encoding of the 'fixed at 95%' reload clamp (inert without a second reload buffer). Nothing must change for GO.
